title: SettingsIPadView
description: Create AggregatorApp/iPad/Settings/SettingsIPadView.swift. Settings list in content column; settings detail (credential entry, about screen, etc.) in detail column driven by selection. Portrait: settings list in detail column; tap pushes settings detail. Reuse existing SettingsViewModel per audit. Handle Empty and Error states where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: Landscape: settings list → detail view flow works
Credential entry and about screen reachable from settings list on iPad

handoff_summary.completed: Created AggregatorApp/iPad/Settings/SettingsIPadView.swift. The file introduces: SettingsSection enum (credentials, about), CredentialsSettingsView private struct (form with server URL, connection test, CF-Access fields), AboutSettingsView private struct (app version/build display), and SettingsIPadView (portrait/landscape dual-mode main view). No other files were touched.
handoff_summary.remaining: N/A — bead scope is fully implemented. AppRootIPad wiring to show SettingsIPadView in the correct split-view column is handled by a downstream bead that integrates all section views.
handoff_summary.risks: Low. The file adds no new framework dependencies and follows established patterns. The SourceKit "No such module UIKit" diagnostic is a false positive that resolves after xcodegen generate is run (all sibling iPad views import UIKit identically). xcodegen project.yml already covers AggregatorApp/iPad recursively, so the new Settings subdirectory is picked up without project.yml changes.
handoff_summary.next_action: Run xcodegen generate and build to confirm the file compiles cleanly. Wire SettingsIPadView into AppRootIPad's content column (alongside the other section views) in the downstream AppRootIPad integration bead.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: Minimal. Only new file added. No modifications to NavigationModel.swift or AppRootIPad.swift means no risk to concurrent sibling beads working on those files.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Chose TodayIPadView's self-contained HStack-for-landscape approach rather than communicating via iPadNavigationModel. Rationale: (1) settings has no dynamic data requiring a shared selection model — selection state is local to the settings pane; (2) avoids modifying NavigationModel.swift and AppRootIPad.swift, keeping bead scope tight; (3) TodayIPadView already validated this pattern for non-list-of-network-items feature tabs. The CredentialsSettingsView is a private struct that duplicates the form from SettingsView intentionally — reusing SettingsView directly would bring its NavigationStack wrapper, causing a nested-NavigationStack issue. AboutSettingsView is minimal (version + build) since the existing SettingsView has no About section; a fuller About screen can be added as a follow-up bead if needed. selectedSection defaults to .credentials so the detail pane is never blank on first render in landscape.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: (1) landscape: tapping Credentials shows the credential form in the detail pane; tapping About shows app version/build; selection highlight updates on the list item. (2) Portrait: tapping Credentials pushes CredentialsSettingsView; back button returns to list; tapping About pushes AboutSettingsView. (3) Rotation from portrait to landscape preserves the selectedSection (it remains in state). (4) Test Connection button in CredentialsSettingsView shows spinner while running and renders success/failure label after. (5) SecureField for Client Secret is masked. (6) No crash when rotating between orientations with a section selected.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: The About screen is intentionally minimal (version + build only). There is no explicit Empty or Error state for the settings list itself — not applicable since the two sections (Credentials, About) are always available without network calls. If the user clears selectedSection externally (which cannot happen in current code), the landscape detail pane falls back to ContentUnavailableView gracefully.

conflict_risks: Minimal. Only new file added. No modifications to NavigationModel.swift or AppRootIPad.swift means no risk to concurrent sibling beads working on those files.

execution_history.summary: Created AggregatorApp/iPad/Settings/SettingsIPadView.swift with self-contained portrait/landscape settings navigation following the same pattern as TodayIPadView. In landscape, an HStack shows a 260px section list (Credentials, About) alongside a detail pane driven by local selectedSection state. In portrait, a NavigationStack handles list → push-to-detail navigation. Credentials detail includes Base URL, Test Connection, and CF-Access fields. About detail shows app version and build number. Existing SettingsView.swift is not modified.

guardrails.template_text:
# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
